PU-1.t: Describe how the respiratory diverticulum (lung bud) arises from ventral foregut endoderm in week 4, and distinguish endodermal airway epithelium and glands from the splanchnic mesoderm that forms cartilage, smooth muscle, and connective tissue.
Explain how the tracheoesophageal ridges fuse to form the tracheoesophageal septum, and relate faulty septation to esophageal atresia with a distal tracheoesophageal fistula.
PU-1.usmle: Respiratory System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: tracheoesophageal fistula

PU-1.t: Sequence the pseudoglandular, canalicular, saccular, and alveolar stages of lung development, and explain why survival with support first becomes possible near the end of the canalicular stage, once respiratory bronchioles and capillaries appear (about weeks 24 to 26).

Explain the timing of surfactant production by type II pneumocytes (beginning in the second trimester and reaching mature levels by about week 35), and interpret an amniotic lecithin to sphingomyelin ratio above 2 as a sign of fetal lung maturity.
Explain how oligohydramnios (for example from bilateral renal agenesis) and congenital diaphragmatic hernia cause pulmonary hypoplasia, and predict respiratory failure at birth.
PU-1.usmle: Respiratory System: Congenital disorders: congenital diaphragmatic hernia

PU-2.t: Trace the change in airway epithelium from pseudostratified ciliated columnar with goblet cells in the trachea and bronchi, to simple cuboidal with club cells in terminal bronchioles, to type I and type II pneumocytes in alveoli.

Distinguish bronchi from bronchioles by the presence of cartilage plates, submucosal glands, and goblet cells, and explain why bronchioles depend on smooth muscle tone and radial traction from surrounding alveoli to stay open.

Describe the functions of type I pneumocytes (thin gas exchange surface), type II pneumocytes (surfactant secretion and regeneration of type I cells), club cells (secretion, cytochrome P450 detoxification, progenitors), and alveolar macrophages.

Explain mucociliary clearance by cilia with a 9 plus 2 microtubule axoneme and dynein arms, and predict how smoking-induced squamous metaplasia or ciliary dysfunction leads to retained mucus and recurrent infection.
Describe the layers of the blood-air barrier (type I pneumocyte, fused basement membranes, capillary endothelium), and relate interstitial fibrosis or edema that thickens it to impaired diffusion.
Identify the nonkeratinized stratified squamous epithelium of the true vocal folds and oropharynx, and relate it to squamous cell carcinoma as the main malignant tumor of the larynx.

PU-3.t: Describe the nasal conchae and meatuses and identify sinus drainage: frontal, maxillary, and anterior ethmoid into the middle meatus; posterior ethmoid into the superior meatus; sphenoid into the sphenoethmoidal recess; nasolacrimal duct into the inferior meatus.

Explain why the maxillary sinus is the sinus most often infected (ostium high on its medial wall, poor gravity drainage), and relate the closeness of maxillary molar roots to its floor to odontogenic sinusitis.
PU-3.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: sinusitis

PU-3.t: Locate Kiesselbach area on the anterior nasal septum, name the arteries that anastomose there (sphenopalatine, anterior ethmoidal, greater palatine, superior labial), and contrast it with posterior epistaxis from sphenopalatine branches.
PU-3.usmle: Respiratory System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: epistaxis

PU-3.t: Describe the nasopharynx, oropharynx, and laryngopharynx, the tonsils of Waldeyer ring, and the pharyngotympanic tube opening, and relate adenoid enlargement to mouth breathing, snoring, and otitis media.

Identify the laryngeal cartilages and intrinsic muscles, state that the posterior cricoarytenoid is the only abductor of the vocal folds, and predict hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve injury, noting that the left nerve loops under the aortic arch.

Distinguish laryngeal innervation by the internal laryngeal nerve (sensation above the vocal folds), external laryngeal nerve (cricothyroid), and recurrent laryngeal nerve (other intrinsic muscles, sensation below the folds), and relate supraglottic sensory loss to aspiration.

PU-4.t: Describe the surface projections of the lungs (ribs 6, 8, and 10) and pleura (ribs 8, 10, and 12) at the midclavicular, midaxillary, and paravertebral lines, and explain why a thoracentesis needle passes just above a rib.

Compare the right lung (three lobes, horizontal and oblique fissures) with the left (two lobes, lingula, cardiac notch), and predict where aspirated material lodges when upright (right lower lobe) or supine (superior segment of right lower lobe).
PU-4.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: aspiration pneumonia

PU-4.t: Identify the relationships of the pulmonary artery, main bronchus, and pulmonary veins at each hilum, noting that the right pulmonary artery lies anterior and the left lies superior to its bronchus.

Describe the superior, anterior, middle, and posterior mediastinum and their contents, and predict typical masses in each, such as thymoma, teratoma, lymphoma, and retrosternal thyroid anteriorly and neurogenic tumors posteriorly.
PU-4.usmle: Respiratory System: Disorders of the pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall: mediastinum

PU-4.t: Compare the pain-sensitive parietal pleura (intercostal and phrenic nerves) with the visceral pleura (autonomic supply), and explain why irritation of the central diaphragmatic pleura refers pain to the shoulder (C3 to C5).
PU-4.usmle: Respiratory System: Disorders of the pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall: pleuritis

PU-4.t: Identify the diaphragmatic openings (inferior vena cava at T8, esophagus and vagal trunks at T10, aorta, thoracic duct, and azygos vein at T12) and the phrenic nerve supply of the diaphragm.
Trace the thoracic duct from the cisterna chyli through the aortic hiatus to the junction of the left subclavian and left internal jugular veins, and relate its injury to chylothorax.
PU-4.usmle: Respiratory System: Disorders of the pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall: chylothorax

PU-5.t: Compare the low-pressure, low-resistance pulmonary circulation with the systemic bronchial circulation, and explain why dual blood supply makes pulmonary infarction uncommon after embolism unless bronchial flow is also compromised.
PU-5.usmle: Respiratory System: Respiratory failure and pulmonary vascular disorders: pulmonary embolism

PU-5.t: Explain hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction, contrast it with hypoxic vasodilation in systemic arterioles, and relate chronic alveolar hypoxia to pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular hypertrophy (cor pulmonale).
PU-5.usmle: Respiratory System: Respiratory failure and pulmonary vascular disorders: pulmonary hypertension

PU-5.t: Describe West zones 1, 2, and 3 by the relationship of alveolar, arterial, and venous pressures, and predict that ventilation-perfusion ratio is highest at the apex, explaining why reactivation tuberculosis favors the apices.
PU-5.usmle: Respiratory System: Metabolic, regulatory, and structural disorders: ventilation-perfusion imbalance

PU-5.t: Trace airflow through the conducting zone (trachea to terminal bronchioles, anatomic dead space about 150 mL) and the respiratory zone (respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts, alveoli), and explain why medium-sized bronchi contribute the most airway resistance.

Apply Poiseuille law to show that airway resistance varies inversely with the fourth power of the radius, and predict how bronchoconstriction, lung volume, and gas density change resistance and airflow.

Explain why pulmonary vascular resistance is lowest at functional residual capacity and rises at low lung volumes (narrowed extra-alveolar vessels) and high lung volumes (compressed alveolar vessels).

PU-6.t: Identify tidal volume, inspiratory and expiratory reserve volumes, residual volume, functional residual capacity, vital capacity, and total lung capacity, and explain why residual volume requires helium dilution or body plethysmography rather than simple spirometry.
Calculate minute and alveolar ventilation, and physiologic dead space with the Bohr equation, and predict why rapid shallow breathing lowers alveolar ventilation at the same minute ventilation.
PU-6.usmle: Respiratory System: Metabolic, regulatory, and structural disorders: hypoventilation

PU-6.t: Explain lung and chest wall compliance, elastic recoil, the negative intrapleural pressure at functional residual capacity, and how surfactant lowers surface tension to stabilize small alveoli according to the law of Laplace.

Interpret spirometry and flow-volume loops to distinguish obstructive disease (reduced FEV1/FVC, normal or increased TLC) from restrictive disease (normal or increased FEV1/FVC, reduced TLC) and fixed upper airway obstruction.

Describe medullary control of breathing (dorsal respiratory group for inspiration, ventral group for forced breathing), the pontine pneumotaxic and apneustic centers, and the Hering-Breuer inflation reflex.

Compare central chemoreceptors, which respond to CSF hydrogen ion generated from arterial CO2, with carotid and aortic body chemoreceptors, which respond mainly to PaO2 below about 60 mmHg, and predict the ventilatory response to hypercapnia and hypoxemia.
PU-6.usmle: Respiratory System: Metabolic, regulatory, and structural disorders: hypoxia

PU-6.t: Distinguish obstructive sleep apnea (pharyngeal collapse despite respiratory effort), central sleep apnea (absent effort), and obesity hypoventilation syndrome (daytime PaCO2 above 45 mmHg with BMI 30 or more), and predict pulmonary hypertension and secondary polycythemia.
PU-6.usmle: Respiratory System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: sleep apnea, obesity-hypoventilation syndrome

PU-7.t: Calculate PAO2 with the alveolar gas equation (PAO2 = FiO2 times (Patm minus 47) minus PaCO2/0.8) and the A-a gradient, and interpret a normal versus a widened gradient.
PU-7.usmle: Respiratory System: Metabolic, regulatory, and structural disorders: disorders of gas exchange

PU-7.t: Classify causes of hypoxemia (low inspired O2, hypoventilation, diffusion limitation, ventilation-perfusion mismatch, right-to-left shunt), and predict which have a normal A-a gradient and which fail to correct with supplemental oxygen.
PU-7.usmle: Respiratory System: Metabolic, regulatory, and structural disorders: hypoxia

PU-7.t: Contrast dead space (V/Q approaching infinity, as in pulmonary embolism) with shunt (V/Q of zero, as in airway obstruction or alveoli filled by pneumonia or edema), and predict the effect of each on PaO2 and PaCO2.
PU-7.usmle: Respiratory System: Metabolic, regulatory, and structural disorders: ventilation-perfusion imbalance

PU-7.t: Apply Fick law of diffusion, distinguish perfusion-limited exchange (N2O, O2 at rest) from diffusion-limited exchange (CO, O2 in fibrosis or strenuous exercise at altitude), and interpret reduced DLCO in emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis.
PU-7.usmle: Respiratory System: Metabolic, regulatory, and structural disorders: disorders of gas exchange

PU-7.t: Distinguish hypoxemia from tissue hypoxia, and classify hypoxia as hypoxemic, anemic, circulatory, or histotoxic (cyanide), predicting PaO2, SaO2, and O2 content in each.
PU-7.usmle: Respiratory System: Metabolic, regulatory, and structural disorders: hypoxia

PU-7.t: Explain acclimatization to high altitude (hyperventilation with respiratory alkalosis, renal bicarbonate excretion, increased erythropoietin and 2,3-BPG, hypoxic pulmonary vasoconstriction) and relate it to acute mountain sickness, high altitude pulmonary edema, and cerebral edema.
PU-7.usmle: Multisystem: Toxins and environmental extremes: decreased atmospheric pressure, high-altitude sickness

PU-8.t: Calculate arterial O2 content (1.34 times Hb times SaO2, plus 0.003 times PaO2), and predict how anemia, polycythemia, and carbon monoxide poisoning change PaO2, SaO2, and O2 content.

Interpret the oxyhemoglobin dissociation curve, explain cooperative binding between T and R states, and name factors that shift it right (increased H+, CO2, temperature, 2,3-BPG) or left (fetal hemoglobin, CO, methemoglobin).
Describe CO2 transport as bicarbonate (about 70 percent), carbaminohemoglobin, and dissolved CO2, including red cell carbonic anhydrase and the chloride shift.
Explain the Bohr effect in tissues and the Haldane effect in the lungs, and relate them to O2 unloading and CO2 loading and unloading.

Explain how carbon monoxide (about 200 times the affinity of O2, left shift) and methemoglobin (ferric iron, chocolate-colored blood) impair O2 delivery, and predict why pulse oximetry misleads while PaO2 stays normal.
PU-8.usmle: Multisystem: Toxins and environmental extremes: gases, vapors, smoke inhalation

PU-8.t: Interpret arterial blood gases in respiratory acidosis and alkalosis, applying expected renal compensation (bicarbonate rises about 1 mEq/L acutely and 3 to 4 mEq/L chronically per 10 mmHg rise in PaCO2), and identify mixed disturbances.
PU-8.usmle: Multisystem: Fluid, electrolyte, and acid-base balance disorders: respiratory acidosis, respiratory alkalosis, mixed acid-base disturbances

PU-9.t: Describe surfactant composition (dipalmitoylphosphatidylcholine as the main lipid, phosphatidylglycerol, surfactant proteins), and explain why fetal cortisol and thyroid hormone promote its synthesis while fetal hyperinsulinemia in maternal diabetes delays it.

Explain the protease and antiprotease balance in the lung, in which alpha-1 antitrypsin inhibits neutrophil elastase, and predict how oxidants in cigarette smoke and recruited neutrophils tip it toward alveolar wall destruction.
PU-9.usmle: Respiratory System: Obstructive airway disease: emphysema

PU-9.t: Relate elastin (cross-linked by copper-dependent lysyl oxidase) to lung recoil, and contrast increased compliance from elastin loss in emphysema with decreased compliance from collagen deposition in fibrosis.

Explain how vitamin A deficiency causes squamous metaplasia of respiratory epithelium and increases respiratory infections, and why pancreatic insufficiency in cystic fibrosis causes deficiency of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K.

Explain how high inspired oxygen concentrations and cigarette smoke generate reactive oxygen species that injure the lung, and describe protection by superoxide dismutase, catalase, and selenium-dependent glutathione peroxidase.
PU-9.usmle: Respiratory System: Adverse effects of drugs: adverse effects of 100% oxygen

PU-9.t: Describe airway mucus as heavily O-glycosylated mucin glycoproteins secreted by goblet cells and submucosal glands, and relate mucous gland hyperplasia in chronic bronchitis and dehydrated mucus in cystic fibrosis to impaired clearance.

PU-10.t: Describe cystic fibrosis as an autosomal recessive CFTR defect on chromosome 7, and explain how the common F508 deletion causes misfolding and proteasomal degradation, reducing chloride secretion and leaving dehydrated, thick airway mucus.
PU-10.usmle: Multisystem: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: cystic fibrosis

PU-10.t: Explain alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (codominant SERPINA1 alleles, PiZZ most severe), and predict panacinar lower lobe emphysema plus cirrhosis with PAS-positive globules from misfolded protein retained in hepatocytes.
PU-10.usmle: Multisystem: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

PU-10.t: Relate dynein arm defects in primary ciliary dyskinesia (autosomal recessive) to bronchiectasis, chronic sinusitis, and infertility, and explain situs inversus in Kartagener syndrome.
PU-10.usmle: Multisystem: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: immotile cilia syndrome (Kartagener syndrome; primary ciliary dyskinesia)

PU-10.t: Describe how p53 and Rb restrain the G1 to S transition, and explain how tobacco carcinogens such as benzo[a]pyrene form DNA adducts that cause mutations, including in TP53.

Identify common driver alterations in lung cancer (EGFR mutations, ALK rearrangements, and KRAS mutations in adenocarcinoma; TP53 and RB1 loss in small cell carcinoma), and relate EGFR mutations to adenocarcinoma in nonsmokers.
PU-10.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: malignant neoplasms of bronchus and lung

PU-11.t: Relate O2 as the final electron acceptor at cytochrome c oxidase (complex IV) to ATP production, and predict the shift to anaerobic glycolysis with lactic acidosis when tissue O2 delivery fails.

Explain how cyanide from burning plastics and carbon monoxide in smoke inhalation inhibit complex IV, and predict lactic acidosis with a normal PaO2 and, in cyanide poisoning, a high venous O2 saturation.
PU-11.usmle: Multisystem: Toxins and environmental extremes: gases, vapors, smoke inhalation

PU-11.t: Calculate the respiratory quotient (CO2 produced divided by O2 consumed) for carbohydrate (1.0), fat (about 0.7), and protein (about 0.8), and predict how fuel mix changes CO2 production and ventilatory demand.
Explain how 2,3-BPG made in the red cell glycolytic shunt lowers hemoglobin O2 affinity, and predict how high altitude and pyruvate kinase deficiency increase 2,3-BPG and O2 unloading.
Relate the increased work of breathing in severe emphysema to higher resting energy expenditure and the weight loss seen in these patients.

PU-12.t: Describe innate lung defenses (nasal filtration, mucociliary escalator, cough, secretory IgA, alveolar macrophages, surfactant proteins A and D acting as opsonins), and relate their impairment by smoking, alcohol, and ciliary defects to pneumonia risk.
PU-12.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: host response to insult

PU-12.t: Explain type I hypersensitivity in allergic asthma and rhinitis, including Th2 cytokines (IL-4 for IgE class switching, IL-5 for eosinophils, IL-13 for mucus), mast cell degranulation, and the early and late phase responses.
PU-12.usmle: Respiratory System: Obstructive airway disease: asthma

PU-12.t: Explain granuloma formation in tuberculosis and sarcoidosis (Th1 cells, IFN-gamma activation of macrophages, TNF-alpha maintenance of granulomas), and predict tuberculosis reactivation when TNF-alpha is blocked.
PU-12.usmle: Multisystem: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: sarcoidosis

PU-12.t: Distinguish hypersensitivity pneumonitis (type III and IV reactions to inhaled organic antigens such as thermophilic actinomycetes in farmer lung, with poorly formed interstitial granulomas) from asthma.
PU-12.usmle: Respiratory System: Pneumoconiosis, fibrosing, restrictive, and interstitial lung disease: hypersensitivity pneumonitis

PU-12.t: Contrast Goodpasture syndrome (type II hypersensitivity against type IV collagen, pulmonary hemorrhage, glomerulonephritis) with granulomatosis with polyangiitis (PR3-ANCA, necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis of upper and lower airways and kidney).
PU-12.usmle: Multisystem: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: Goodpasture syndrome, granulomatosis with polyangiitis

PU-12.t: Explain how toxoid vaccines (diphtheria, tetanus), acellular pertussis vaccine, and polysaccharide-protein conjugate vaccines (Haemophilus influenzae type b, pneumococcus) induce protection, contrasting T-cell independent polysaccharide responses with T-cell dependent conjugate responses.

Explain how lung cancers evade immunity by reducing MHC class I and expressing PD-L1, and relate antibodies to shared tumor and neural antigens (anti-Hu, anti-voltage-gated calcium channel) to paraneoplastic neurologic syndromes.

PU-13.t: Describe Streptococcus pneumoniae (gram-positive lancet-shaped diplococci, alpha-hemolytic, optochin sensitive, bile soluble, polysaccharide capsule, IgA protease) as the most common cause of community-acquired and lobar pneumonia.
PU-13.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: community-acquired pneumonia

PU-13.t: Compare gram-negative respiratory pathogens: Haemophilus influenzae (needs factors X and V), Klebsiella pneumoniae (mucoid capsule, alcoholics), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (oxidase positive, cystic fibrosis and ventilated patients), and Legionella (charcoal yeast extract agar, contaminated water).
PU-13.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: pneumonia

PU-13.t: Explain the toxins of Corynebacterium diphtheriae (prophage-encoded, ADP-ribosylates EF-2) and Bordetella pertussis (ADP-ribosylates Gi, raising cAMP), and link each to its clinical picture.
PU-13.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: Bordetella pertussis

PU-13.t: Describe Mycobacterium tuberculosis (acid-fast mycolic acid wall, cord factor, sulfatides), its spread by airborne droplet nuclei, and its survival in macrophages by blocking phagolysosome fusion.
PU-13.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: pulmonary tuberculosis

PU-13.t: Compare influenza (segmented negative-sense RNA, hemagglutinin and neuraminidase, antigenic drift and shift), respiratory syncytial virus (a pneumovirus, formerly classed as a paramyxovirus, whose F protein forms syncytia), and coronaviruses (enveloped positive-sense RNA; SARS-CoV-2 spike binds ACE2).
PU-13.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: viral infection

PU-13.t: Distinguish the dimorphic fungi by geography and tissue form: Histoplasma (Ohio and Mississippi valleys, bird and bat droppings, small yeasts in macrophages), Blastomyces (Great Lakes and Ohio and Mississippi basins, broad-based budding yeast), and Coccidioides (southwestern United States, spherules with endospores).
PU-13.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: fungal infection

PU-13.t: Identify Aspergillus (septate hyphae branching at acute angles) and Pneumocystis jirovecii (cysts on methenamine silver stain), and relate each to the host defect that allows infection (neutropenia, CD4 count below 200 cells/mm3).
PU-13.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: fungal infection

PU-14-A.t: Explain neonatal respiratory distress syndrome (surfactant deficiency from prematurity, maternal diabetes, or cesarean delivery) leading to atelectasis and hyaline membranes, and predict patent ductus arteriosus, plus bronchopulmonary dysplasia and retinopathy of prematurity from oxygen therapy.

Explain acute respiratory distress syndrome as diffuse alveolar damage after sepsis, pneumonia, aspiration, trauma, or pancreatitis, with neutrophil-mediated capillary leak, hyaline membranes, bilateral infiltrates, and hypoxemia (PaO2/FiO2 of 300 or less) not explained by heart failure.
PU-14-A.usmle: Respiratory System: Respiratory failure and pulmonary vascular disorders: acute respiratory distress syndrome

PU-14-A.t: Describe idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (repeated alveolar epithelial injury with TGF-beta driven fibrosis), its usual interstitial pneumonia pattern (patchy subpleural and basal fibrosis, fibroblastic foci, honeycombing), clubbing, and restrictive spirometry with reduced DLCO.
PU-14-A.usmle: Respiratory System: Pneumoconiosis, fibrosing, restrictive, and interstitial lung disease: usual interstitial pneumonia

PU-14-A.t: Compare pneumoconioses: coal workers (upper lobes, progressive massive fibrosis), silicosis (upper lobes, eggshell calcified hilar nodes, tuberculosis risk), asbestosis (lower lobes, ferruginous bodies), and berylliosis (noncaseating granulomas, aerospace work).
PU-14-A.usmle: Respiratory System: Pneumoconiosis, fibrosing, restrictive, and interstitial lung disease: pneumoconiosis, asbestosis, silicosis, berylliosis

PU-14-A.t: Describe sarcoidosis (noncaseating granulomas, bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, elevated ACE, hypercalcemia from macrophage 1-alpha-hydroxylase), its higher incidence in Black women, and Lofgren syndrome (erythema nodosum, hilar lymphadenopathy, arthritis, fever).
PU-14-A.usmle: Multisystem: Immunologic and inflammatory disorders: sarcoidosis, Lofgren syndrome

PU-14-A.t: Distinguish intrinsic restrictive disease (reduced DLCO) from extrapulmonary restriction caused by obesity, kyphoscoliosis, or neuromuscular weakness (usually normal DLCO and a normal A-a gradient with hypoventilation).
PU-14-A.usmle: Respiratory System: Metabolic, regulatory, and structural disorders: hypoventilation

PU-14-A.t: Distinguish desquamative interstitial pneumonia (smokers, macrophages filling alveoli), nonspecific interstitial pneumonia (uniform interstitial inflammation and fibrosis), and cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (polypoid fibroblast plugs, Masson bodies).
PU-14-A.usmle: Respiratory System: Pneumoconiosis, fibrosing, restrictive, and interstitial lung disease: interstitial pneumonia; Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: bronchiolitis obliterans with organizing pneumonia

PU-14-A.t: Identify occupational causes of lung disease: byssinosis (cotton dust), bagassosis (moldy sugarcane, hypersensitivity pneumonitis), and silo-filler disease (nitrogen dioxide causing bronchiolitis and pulmonary edema).
PU-14-A.usmle: Respiratory System: Pneumoconiosis, fibrosing, restrictive, and interstitial lung disease: byssinosis, bagassosis, silo-filler's lung

PU-14-A.t: Identify bleomycin, amiodarone, busulfan, and methotrexate as causes of drug-induced pulmonary fibrosis to be distinguished from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
PU-14-A.usmle: Respiratory System: Adverse effects of drugs: bleomycin, amiodarone

PU-14-B.t: Explain asthma pathogenesis (atopic Th2 inflammation and nonatopic triggers such as viral infection, cold air, exercise, and aspirin), and identify Curschmann spirals, Charcot-Leyden crystals, goblet cell hyperplasia, basement membrane thickening, and smooth muscle hypertrophy.
PU-14-B.usmle: Respiratory System: Obstructive airway disease: asthma

PU-14-B.t: Predict findings in acute asthma (wheezing, prolonged expiration, pulsus paradoxus, reversible obstruction on spirometry), and interpret a normal or rising PaCO2 after early respiratory alkalosis as a sign of tiring and impending respiratory failure.
PU-14-B.usmle: Respiratory System: Obstructive airway disease: asthma, reactive airway disease

PU-14-B.t: Explain bronchiectasis as permanent airway dilation from obstruction plus necrotizing infection, identify causes (cystic fibrosis, primary ciliary dyskinesia, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis, tumor or foreign body), and predict copious purulent sputum, hemoptysis, clubbing, and amyloidosis.
PU-14-B.usmle: Respiratory System: Obstructive airway disease: bronchiectasis

PU-14-B.t: Describe chronic bronchitis (productive cough for at least 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years), mucous gland hyperplasia with a Reid index above 0.5, and the hypoxemia, hypercapnia, cyanosis, and cor pulmonale of the blue bloater.
PU-14-B.usmle: Respiratory System: Obstructive airway disease: chronic bronchitis

PU-14-B.t: Compare centriacinar emphysema (smoking, upper lobes), panacinar emphysema (alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency, lower lobes), and paraseptal emphysema (subpleural bullae, spontaneous pneumothorax in young adults), and predict barrel chest, air trapping, and pursed-lip breathing.
PU-14-B.usmle: Respiratory System: Obstructive airway disease: emphysema

PU-14-B.t: Interpret COPD testing (FEV1/FVC below 0.7, increased TLC and residual volume), and contrast DLCO and blood gases in predominant emphysema (low DLCO, near normal gases until late) with predominant chronic bronchitis (normal DLCO, early hypoxemia and hypercapnia).
PU-14-B.usmle: Respiratory System: Obstructive airway disease: chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

PU-14-C.t: Explain acute bronchitis as a mostly viral, self-limited inflammation of the large airways causing cough for up to about 3 weeks, and distinguish it from pneumonia (no consolidation) and from chronic bronchitis.
PU-14-C.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: bronchitis (acute)

PU-14-C.t: Describe epiglottitis (classically Haemophilus influenzae type b in unvaccinated children) with sudden fever, drooling, dysphagia, muffled voice, tripod posture, and a thumb sign on lateral neck radiograph, and predict sudden airway obstruction.
PU-14-C.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: epiglottitis

PU-14-C.t: Distinguish acute laryngitis (usually viral, hoarseness) from croup (parainfluenza virus laryngotracheobronchitis, barking cough, inspiratory stridor, steeple sign) and bacterial tracheitis (toxic child, purulent tracheal secretions, often Staphylococcus aureus).
PU-14-C.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: acute laryngitis, croup, tracheitis

PU-14-C.t: Compare allergic rhinitis (IgE, eosinophils, pale boggy mucosa, seasonal or perennial) with infectious rhinitis (rhinovirus, an acid-labile picornavirus binding ICAM-1, as the main cause of the common cold) and nonallergic vasomotor rhinitis.
PU-14-C.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: rhinitis, viral infections (rhinoviruses)

PU-14-C.t: Explain sinusitis from ostial obstruction (mostly viral; bacterial Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis), and predict complications such as orbital cellulitis, cavernous sinus thrombosis, and mucormycosis in diabetic ketoacidosis.
PU-14-C.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: sinusitis

PU-14-C.t: Distinguish Streptococcus pyogenes pharyngitis (beta-hemolytic, bacitracin sensitive, M protein; fever, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior nodes, no cough) from viral pharyngitis, and predict rheumatic fever (molecular mimicry) and poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis.
PU-14-C.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: pharyngitis, streptococcal throat infections

PU-14-C.t: Distinguish streptococcal tonsillitis from infectious mononucleosis (EBV, exudative tonsillitis, posterior cervical nodes, atypical lymphocytes, heterophile antibodies, splenomegaly), and predict peritonsillar abscess (uvular deviation, trismus, muffled voice).
PU-14-C.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: tonsillitis, peritonsillar abscess

PU-14-D.t: Explain chylothorax from thoracic duct disruption (trauma, surgery, lymphoma), and identify milky pleural fluid with triglycerides above 110 mg/dL and chylomicrons.
PU-14-D.usmle: Respiratory System: Disorders of the pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall: chylothorax

PU-14-D.t: Describe hemothorax from chest trauma, vascular rupture, or malignancy, define it by a pleural fluid hematocrit at least half the blood hematocrit, and predict hypovolemic shock and later fibrothorax.
PU-14-D.usmle: Respiratory System: Disorders of the pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall: hemothorax

PU-14-D.t: Explain obstructive (resorption) atelectasis from absorption of trapped alveolar air beyond a mucus plug, tumor, or foreign body, predict mediastinal shift toward the collapse, and contrast compression atelectasis, which shifts the mediastinum away.
PU-14-D.usmle: Respiratory System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: atelectasis

PU-14-D.t: Describe asbestos-related pleural disease (calcified parietal pleural plaques, effusion, diffuse pleural fibrosis), ferruginous bodies, and the increased risk of bronchogenic carcinoma (synergistic with smoking) and mesothelioma.
PU-14-D.usmle: Respiratory System: Pneumoconiosis, fibrosing, restrictive, and interstitial lung disease: asbestosis

PU-14-D.t: Compare primary spontaneous pneumothorax (tall thin young men, ruptured apical blebs), secondary pneumothorax (COPD, cystic fibrosis), and tension pneumothorax (tracheal deviation away, hypotension, distended neck veins), and predict hyperresonance with absent breath sounds.
PU-14-D.usmle: Respiratory System: Disorders of the pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall: pneumothorax

PU-14-D.t: Classify pleural effusions with Light criteria (exudate if pleural to serum protein above 0.5, LDH ratio above 0.6, or LDH above two thirds of the serum upper limit), and identify transudative (heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome) versus exudative causes.
PU-14-D.usmle: Respiratory System: Disorders of the pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall: pleural effusion

PU-14-D.t: Identify empyema (purulent exudate after pneumonia), mediastinitis (esophageal perforation, sternotomy, inhalational anthrax), pneumomediastinum (subcutaneous crepitus, Hamman crunch), and costochondritis (reproducible chest wall tenderness).
PU-14-D.usmle: Respiratory System: Disorders of the pleura, mediastinum, and chest wall: empyema, mediastinitis, pneumomediastinum, costochondritis

PU-14-D.t: Predict findings of chest trauma: flail chest (paradoxical segment motion), pulmonary contusion (hemorrhage with worsening hypoxemia), open pneumothorax from a penetrating wound, and diaphragmatic rupture (bowel in the left hemithorax).
PU-14-D.usmle: Respiratory System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: diaphragm/chest wall injury, penetrating chest wounds, pulmonary contusion

PU-14-E.t: Explain pulmonary edema using Starling forces, contrasting cardiogenic edema (raised capillary hydrostatic pressure, wedge pressure above 18 mmHg, hemosiderin-laden macrophages) with noncardiogenic edema from capillary injury, low oncotic pressure, or lymphatic obstruction.
PU-14-E.usmle: Respiratory System: Respiratory failure and pulmonary vascular disorders: pulmonary edema

PU-14-E.t: Explain pulmonary embolism from deep vein thrombosis (Virchow triad), and predict sudden dyspnea, pleuritic pain, tachycardia, hypoxemia with respiratory alkalosis, a widened A-a gradient, raised D-dimer, and acute right heart strain with saddle emboli.
PU-14-E.usmle: Respiratory System: Respiratory failure and pulmonary vascular disorders: pulmonary embolism

PU-14-E.t: Distinguish fat embolism (long bone fracture, hypoxemia, neurologic changes, petechial rash within 24 to 72 hours), air embolism (venous catheters, diving decompression), and amniotic fluid embolism (sudden collapse and DIC during delivery).
PU-14-E.usmle: Respiratory System: Respiratory failure and pulmonary vascular disorders: air and fat embolism

PU-14-E.t: Describe pulmonary infarction as a wedge-shaped hemorrhagic infarct based on the pleura, occurring when an embolus blocks a medium or small artery and bronchial flow is reduced (as in heart failure), and predict hemoptysis and pleuritic pain.
PU-14-E.usmle: Respiratory System: Respiratory failure and pulmonary vascular disorders: pulmonary embolism

PU-14-E.t: Classify pulmonary hypertension (pulmonary arterial including BMPR2 mutation, left heart disease, lung disease or hypoxia, chronic thromboembolism), and describe medial hypertrophy, intimal fibrosis, plexiform lesions, and progression to cor pulmonale.
PU-14-E.usmle: Respiratory System: Respiratory failure and pulmonary vascular disorders: pulmonary hypertension

PU-14-E.t: Describe pulmonary arteriovenous malformations in hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (autosomal dominant), and predict hypoxemia from right-to-left shunting, hemoptysis, and paradoxical embolic stroke or brain abscess.
PU-14-E.usmle: Respiratory System: Respiratory failure and pulmonary vascular disorders: arteriovenous fistula

PU-14-F.t: Describe adenocarcinoma as the most common lung cancer overall and in nonsmokers and women, typically peripheral and mucin producing, and identify adenocarcinoma in situ by lepidic growth along alveolar walls without invasion.

Describe bronchial carcinoid as a low-grade neuroendocrine tumor (nests of uniform cells, chromogranin positive, often a central polypoid mass, not linked to smoking) that may obstruct a bronchus and rarely produces carcinoid syndrome.
PU-14-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: bronchial carcinoid tumors

PU-14-F.t: Compare esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (upper and middle third; smoking, alcohol, very hot drinks, achalasia, nitrosamines) with adenocarcinoma (distal third; GERD, Barrett esophagus, obesity), and predict progressive dysphagia, weight loss, and tracheoesophageal fistula.

Describe laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (smoking and alcohol, early hoarseness when glottic), and contrast it with benign vocal fold nodules from voice overuse and juvenile laryngeal papillomatosis from HPV types 6 and 11.
PU-14-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: larynx; vocal cord polyps, juvenile papillomatosis

PU-14-F.t: Describe malignant mesothelioma (asbestos exposure decades earlier, no smoking link, recurrent hemorrhagic effusion, tumor encasing the lung, calretinin and cytokeratin positive, long slender microvilli), and distinguish it from metastatic pleural adenocarcinoma.
PU-14-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: mesothelioma; secondary malignant neoplasms of pleura

PU-14-F.t: Describe nasopharyngeal carcinoma (EBV association, higher incidence in southern China and parts of Africa, nonkeratinizing or undifferentiated histology), and predict cervical lymph node metastasis and unilateral serous otitis media from eustachian tube blockage.
PU-14-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: head and neck cancer

PU-14-F.t: Explain nasal polyps (chronic rhinosinusitis, allergy, aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease with asthma, cystic fibrosis in a child) and vocal fold polyps (voice strain, smoking), and predict nasal obstruction, anosmia, and hoarseness.
PU-14-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: nasal polyps, vocal cord polyps

PU-14-F.t: Describe small cell carcinoma (central, strongly linked to smoking, small neuroendocrine cells with scant cytoplasm and nuclear molding, chromogranin and synaptophysin positive), and predict early metastasis and ACTH, ADH, and Lambert-Eaton paraneoplastic syndromes.

Compare non-small-cell carcinomas: squamous cell (central, smoking, keratin pearls, intercellular bridges, cavitation, PTHrP hypercalcemia) and large cell (peripheral, poorly differentiated, poor prognosis), alongside adenocarcinoma.
PU-14-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: squamous cell, large cell

PU-14-F.t: Match lung cancer paraneoplastic syndromes to type: PTHrP hypercalcemia (squamous cell), ACTH Cushing syndrome and SIADH (small cell), Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome (small cell), and hypertrophic pulmonary osteoarthropathy with clubbing (especially adenocarcinoma).
PU-14-F.usmle: Multisystem: Paraneoplastic syndromes: SIADH, Cushing syndrome, hypercalcemia of malignancy, myasthenic syndrome, pulmonary osteoarthropathy

PU-14-F.t: Predict local effects of lung cancer spread: superior sulcus (Pancoast) tumor with Horner syndrome and brachial plexus deficits, superior vena cava syndrome, hoarseness from recurrent laryngeal nerve invasion, and diaphragm elevation from phrenic nerve invasion.
PU-14-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: malignant neoplasms of bronchus and lung

PU-14-F.t: Distinguish metastases to the lung (multiple well-circumscribed nodules, more common than primary lung cancer) from a benign hamartoma (cartilage and fat, popcorn calcification) when evaluating a solitary pulmonary nodule.
PU-14-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: solitary pulmonary nodule; secondary malignant neoplasms of lung

PU-14-F.t: Relate HPV type 16 to oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma of the tonsil and base of tongue, and contrast it with tobacco and alcohol related squamous carcinoma of the oral cavity and pharynx.
PU-14-F.usmle: Respiratory System: Neoplasms: lip, oral cavity, and pharynx; head and neck cancer

PU-14-G.t: Predict the clinical picture of cystic fibrosis: meconium ileus, pancreatic insufficiency with steatorrhea, chronic Pseudomonas and Staphylococcus aureus infection, bronchiectasis, nasal polyps, male infertility from absent vas deferens, and sweat chloride of 60 mmol/L or higher.
PU-14-G.usmle: Multisystem: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: cystic fibrosis

PU-14-G.t: Explain why sweat is salty in cystic fibrosis (failed chloride reabsorption in the sweat duct) while airway surface liquid is depleted (failed chloride secretion with excess sodium absorption through ENaC).
PU-14-G.usmle: Multisystem: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: cystic fibrosis

PU-14-G.t: Describe tracheoesophageal fistula, most often esophageal atresia with a distal fistula, and predict polyhydramnios, drooling, choking and cyanosis with feeds, a gastric air bubble, and failure to pass a nasogastric tube, noting the VACTERL association.
PU-14-G.usmle: Respiratory System: Traumatic and mechanical disorders: tracheoesophageal fistula; Multisystem: Genetic, metabolic, and developmental disorders: VACTERL association

PU-14-G.t: Describe congenital diaphragmatic hernia (usually left posterolateral, failed pleuroperitoneal fold closure) with abdominal contents in the chest, pulmonary hypoplasia, and a scaphoid abdomen at birth.
PU-14-G.usmle: Respiratory System: Congenital disorders: congenital diaphragmatic hernia

PU-14-G.t: Distinguish pulmonary sequestration (nonfunctioning lung tissue with systemic arterial supply from the aorta and no bronchial connection) from bronchogenic cyst (abnormal foregut budding, fluid-filled, usually mediastinal), and predict recurrent infection.
PU-14-G.usmle: Respiratory System: Congenital disorders: pulmonary sequestration, bronchogenic cysts, congenital cysts

PU-14-H.t: Compare lobar pneumonia (Streptococcus pneumoniae, Klebsiella; congestion, red hepatization, gray hepatization, resolution; dullness, egophony, increased fremitus) with bronchopneumonia (Staphylococcus aureus, Haemophilus influenzae, Pseudomonas; patchy, often multilobar, centered on bronchioles).
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: community-acquired pneumonia, bronchopneumonia

PU-14-H.t: Describe atypical pneumonia (Mycoplasma pneumoniae, which lacks a cell wall, with cold agglutinins in young adults in close quarters; Chlamydia pneumoniae; Legionella with hyponatremia and diarrhea; viruses), and predict patchy interstitial infiltrates that look worse than the patient.
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: pneumonia (Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydophila pneumoniae, Legionella)

PU-14-H.t: Describe diphtheria (gray adherent pseudomembrane that bleeds when scraped, bull neck lymphadenopathy, tellurite agar, Elek test) and predict toxin-mediated myocarditis, heart block, and cranial and peripheral neuropathy.
Describe endemic fungal pneumonia (histoplasmosis, blastomycosis, coccidioidomycosis) in healthy hosts, and predict dissemination to skin, bone, and meninges, and granulomas mimicking tuberculosis.
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: fungal infection (histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis)

PU-14-H.t: Distinguish Pneumocystis pneumonia (CD4 below 200, bilateral ground-glass infiltrates, exertional hypoxemia, high LDH) from aspergillosis (aspergilloma in an old cavity, angioinvasive disease in neutropenia, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis in asthma and cystic fibrosis).
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: fungal infection (aspergillosis, Pneumocystis jirovecii)

PU-14-H.t: Explain lung abscess from aspiration of oropharyngeal anaerobes (Bacteroides, Fusobacterium, Peptostreptococcus) in alcoholism, seizures, or dysphagia, and predict an air-fluid level in dependent segments and foul-smelling sputum; identify Staphylococcus aureus and Klebsiella as other causes.
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: lung abscess, aspiration pneumonia

PU-14-H.t: Describe the catarrhal, paroxysmal (inspiratory whoop, posttussive vomiting), and convalescent stages of pertussis, its marked lymphocytosis, and apnea and pneumonia in young infants.
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: Bordetella pertussis pneumonia

PU-14-H.t: Describe respiratory syncytial virus as the most common cause of bronchiolitis and pneumonia in infants (winter epidemics, wheezing, tachypnea), and identify prematurity and congenital heart or lung disease as risk factors for severe disease.
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: acute bronchiolitis; respiratory syncytial virus

PU-14-H.t: Trace primary tuberculosis from the Ghon focus and hilar node (Ghon complex) with caseating granulomas to latent infection, and interpret tuberculin skin test and interferon-gamma release assay results.
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: pulmonary tuberculosis

PU-14-H.t: Predict secondary (reactivation) tuberculosis in the apices with cavitation, fever, night sweats, weight loss, and hemoptysis, and miliary spread to kidneys, meninges, and vertebrae (Pott disease), especially with HIV or immunosuppression.

Describe coronavirus disease: common cold strains, and SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 (SARS-CoV-2 entry via ACE2 on airway and alveolar cells, loss of smell, diffuse alveolar damage, thrombosis), and identify older age and comorbidity as risk factors.
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: viral infections (coronaviruses)

PU-14-H.t: Identify likely organisms in hospital-acquired and ventilator-associated pneumonia (Pseudomonas, MRSA, enteric gram-negative rods), and distinguish chemical aspiration pneumonitis from bacterial aspiration pneumonia.
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: hospital-acquired pneumonia, ventilator-associated pneumonia, pneumonitis

PU-14-H.t: Explain influenza pneumonia and predict secondary bacterial pneumonia with Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pneumoniae, and identify avian influenza as a source of novel strains through reassortment.
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: viral infection (influenza A, influenza B, H1N1, avian influenza)

PU-14-H.t: Identify zoonotic and bioterrorism causes of pneumonia: inhalational anthrax (hemorrhagic mediastinitis, widened mediastinum), tularemia (rabbits, ticks), Q fever (Coxiella from farm animal birth products), and melioidosis (Burkholderia pseudomallei, Southeast Asia).
PU-14-H.usmle: Respiratory System: Infectious, immunologic, and inflammatory disorders: anthrax, Francisella tularensis, Coxiella burnetii, Burkholderia pseudomallei
